recognize_zh: 分葉核中性球的細胞質邊緣可見一個淡藍灰色、邊界模糊的橢圓形包涵體（紅箭頭），同時伴有毒性顆粒與空泡，符合 Döhle 小體。
features: Segmented neutrophil (~14 µm) with a pale blue-grey, poorly demarcated oval cytoplasmic inclusion near the cell membrane (red arrow)
Coarse, dark toxic granulation throughout the cytoplasm
Normal nuclear segmentation (3 lobes) with condensed chromatin
Background red cells without obvious giant platelets in this field
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows a segmented neutrophil containing a small, pale blue-grey, oval cytoplasmic inclusion at the periphery of the cell, consistent with a Döhle body. The same cell shows coarse toxic granulation and cytoplasmic vacuoles. No giant platelets are present in this field. Findings are consistent with toxic (reactive) neutrophil changes, as seen in sepsis, burns, or severe inflammation.

ddx.vs: MYH9 inclusions are larger, more spindle-shaped and sharply defined, occur without toxic granulation or vacuoles, and are accompanied by giant platelets and thrombocytopenia.
Morulae are dark blue-purple, stippled mulberry-like clusters rather than a pale homogeneous blue-grey smudge.
Chediak-Higashi granules are giant, discrete, azurophilic/grey granules rather than a pale, ill-defined ribosomal patch.
Engulfed organisms are sharply outlined cocci, rods or yeasts, often within vacuoles, and are more darkly stained.
